public: Anyone, from any class, is allowed to use this.
private: Only code inside this same class can use this. It is hidden from everyone else.
protected: Usable inside this class, its child classes, and its package.
static: Belongs to the class itself, not to one object. There is one shared copy, and you use it without calling new.
final: Cannot be changed after it is set. A final field is given a value once and then stays the same.
class: A blueprint. It describes the data (fields) and actions (methods) that its objects will have.
interface: A contract: a list of methods a class promises to have, without saying how they work. Like a plug socket shape that many plugs can fit.
implements: This class keeps the promise of an interface by writing real code for all of its methods.
extends: This class is a child of another class and gets all of its code for free, then can add or change things.
abstract: Not complete on its own. An abstract class or method must be finished by a child class before it can be used.
enum: A fixed list of named values, for example CLOSED, OPEN, HALF_OPEN. Nothing outside the list is allowed.
record: A short way to make a simple data class. Java writes the constructor, getters, equals and toString for you, and the values cannot change.
sealed: Only the classes listed after permits are allowed to extend or implement this.
permits: The exact list of classes allowed to extend a sealed class or interface.
new: Creates a fresh object from a class. new User() means: build one User now.
this: Means the current object. this.name is the name field of the object we are inside.
return: Stop the method here and hand this value back to whoever called it.
void: This method does some work but gives nothing back.
synchronized: Only one thread may run this code at a time. Others wait their turn, like a single key to a room.
volatile: Every thread always sees the latest value of this field, never an old cached copy.
throw: Raise an error right now. The normal flow stops and the error travels up until someone catches it.
throws: A warning label on a method: this method may raise these kinds of errors.
try: Run this code, but be ready: if it fails, jump to the catch block instead of crashing.
catch: What to do when the code in try fails with this kind of error.
finally: This block always runs at the end, whether the try worked or failed. Good for cleanup.
null: Means 'nothing here'. A variable that points to no object.
var: Let Java work out the type from the value on the right, so you don't have to write it.
switch: Choose one branch based on a value, like a menu: case A do this, case B do that.
boolean: A yes/no value: true or false.
int: A whole number like 5 or -3 (up to about 2 billion).
long: A whole number that can be much bigger than int. Used for ids and times in milliseconds.
double: A number with a decimal point, like 99.5.
Object: The parent of every class in Java. Object can hold anything.
List: An ordered collection of items, like a numbered shopping list. List<User> means a list of User objects.
Map: A lookup table of key → value pairs, like a dictionary: word → meaning.
HashMap: The everyday Map. Fast lookup by key, but not safe for many threads at once.
ConcurrentHashMap: A Map that many threads can read and write at the same time safely.
CopyOnWriteArrayList: A thread-safe list. Every change makes a fresh copy, so loops over it never break.
Optional: A box that may or may not contain a value. It forces you to handle the 'not found' case instead of getting a null surprise.
UUID: A random, practically unique id like 7f9c24e8-3b12-4d0a-...
Duration: An amount of time, like 2 seconds or 10 minutes.
LocalDate: A calendar date without a time, like 2026-05-12.
Supplier: A small function that takes nothing and gives back a value. Used to pass 'code to run later'.
Consumer: A small function that takes a value and returns nothing, for example 'print this'.
Runnable: A piece of code that can be run later, with no input and no output.
Comparator: A rule that says which of two items comes first. Used for sorting.
CompletableFuture: A promise of a result that will arrive later, usually computed on another thread.
ExecutorService: A pool of worker threads. You give it tasks and it runs them.
Executors: A helper that creates ready-made thread pools.
Semaphore: A counter of permits. Only N threads can hold a permit at once; the rest are turned away or wait.
AtomicLong: A number that many threads can increase safely without locks.
ThreadLocal: A variable where each thread has its own separate value.
ThreadLocalRandom: A fast random-number generator for the current thread.
Thread: A separate line of work running at the same time as others.
Collectors: Helpers that turn a stream back into a List, Map, etc.
stream: Turns a collection into a pipeline where you can filter, map and collect items step by step.
Override: Marks a method that replaces a method from the parent class or interface. Java checks you spelled it right.
@Override: Marks a method that replaces a method from the parent class or interface. Java checks you spelled it right.
@SpringBootApplication: The starting point of a Spring Boot app. It turns on auto-configuration and scans your package for beans.
@Component: Tells Spring: create one object of this class and manage it for me (it becomes a 'bean').
@Service: Same as @Component, but the name says this class holds business logic.
@Repository: Same as @Component, for classes that talk to the database. Spring also converts database errors into friendly Spring errors.
@RestController: This class answers web (HTTP) requests and sends back data, usually JSON.
@Configuration: This class contains setup code. Its @Bean methods create objects for Spring to manage.
@Bean: The object returned by this method is handed to Spring, which keeps it and injects it wherever it is needed.
@Autowired: Asks Spring to fill this in with the right bean. With a single constructor you don't need it.
@Value: Reads a value from application.properties / yml, for example @Value("${shop.discount}").
@Primary: If there are several beans of the same type, use this one by default.
@Qualifier: Pick a specific bean by its name when there are several of the same type.
@Scope: Controls how many objects Spring makes. Default is one (singleton); "prototype" means a new one every time.
@RequestMapping: The base web address for all endpoints in this controller, like /orders.
@GetMapping: This method answers HTTP GET requests (reading data) at this address.
@PostMapping: This method answers HTTP POST requests (creating something) at this address.
@PathVariable: Takes a value from the URL itself. In /orders/{id}, the {id} part.
@RequestParam: Takes a value from the query string, like ?amount=500.
@RequestBody: Turns the JSON sent by the client into a Java object.
@RequestHeader: Reads an HTTP header sent by the client, like Idempotency-Key.
@Header: Reads a header from a Kafka/messaging message.
@Transactional: Run this method as one database transaction: if anything fails, all its database changes are undone together.
@EventListener: Run this method whenever an event of this type is published inside the app.
@TransactionalEventListener: Like @EventListener, but runs only after the database transaction has really committed.
@Async: Run this method on a background thread so the caller doesn't wait.
@EnableAsync: Switches on support for @Async in the app.
@Order: Sets the order when several beans or listeners run for the same thing. Lower number runs first.
@Cacheable: Remember the result. Next time with the same input, return the saved result without running the method.
@CacheEvict: Remove a saved result from the cache, usually after the data changes.
@EnableCaching: Switches on support for @Cacheable and friends.
@Scheduled: Run this method automatically on a timer, like every 5 seconds or every night at 2 AM.
@Aspect: This class adds extra behaviour (like logging or timing) around other methods without changing them.
@Around: Run this code before and after the matching methods. pjp.proceed() calls the real method.
@EnableEurekaServer: Turns this app into a service registry (the phone book other services register in).
@LoadBalanced: Lets this HTTP client call a service by name and spread calls over its instances.
@FeignClient: Write an interface, and Spring creates the HTTP client that calls the other service for you.
@KafkaListener: Run this method for every message that arrives on these Kafka topics.
@RetryableTopic: If handling a message fails, retry it later through separate retry topics, then send it to the dead letter topic.
@DltHandler: Runs for messages that ended up in the dead letter topic.
@Retryable: If this method throws one of these errors, call it again automatically.
@Backoff: How long to wait between retries, and how much longer each time.
@Recover: The backup method that runs when all retries have failed.
@CircuitBreaker: Wraps the method in a circuit breaker: if calls keep failing, stop calling and use the fallback method.
@Retry: Retries the method using the settings with this name in application.yml.
@Bulkhead: Limits how many calls to this method can run at the same time.
@RateLimiter: Limits how many calls to this method are allowed per time period.
@TimeLimiter: Gives up if the method takes longer than the configured time.
@SchedulerLock: Makes sure a @Scheduled job runs on only one server, even if you run many copies of the app.
@Entity: This class is stored in a database table. Each object is one row.
@Table: Sets the database table name (and extra rules like unique columns).
@Id: This field is the primary key: the unique id of each row.
@GeneratedValue: Let the database create the id automatically (1, 2, 3...).
@Column: Settings for one column, for example unique = true.
@Version: A number that goes up on every update. If two people update the same row at once, the second one gets an error instead of silently overwriting.
@Lob: Store this as a large text/binary column, for long JSON etc.
@Enumerated: Store an enum in the database, usually as its name like "HELD".
@UniqueConstraint: The database will reject two rows with the same values in these columns.
@Query: Write your own query for a repository method instead of letting Spring guess from the name.
@Param: Connects a method parameter to a :name placeholder in @Query.
@EntityGraph: Load related data in the same query, to avoid the N+1 query problem.
@Getter: Lombok writes all the getX() methods for you.
@Setter: Lombok writes all the setX() methods for you.
@Builder: Lombok writes a builder so you can create objects with .builder().name(...).build().
@RequiredArgsConstructor: Lombok writes a constructor for all final fields. Spring then uses it to inject dependencies.
@NoArgsConstructor: Lombok writes an empty constructor (JPA needs one).
@AllArgsConstructor: Lombok writes a constructor that takes every field.
@Slf4j: Lombok adds a ready-to-use logger called log, so you can write log.info(...).
@Test: This method is a test. The test runner runs it and reports pass or fail.
@Mock: Create a fake version of this class for the test. You decide what it returns.
@ExtendWith: Plug extra powers into the test class, here Mockito support.
@JsonProperty: The JSON field with this exact name goes into this Java field.
@JsonIgnoreProperties: Don't fail if the JSON has extra fields we don't know about.
JpaRepository: Extend this interface and Spring writes save, findById, findAll, delete and more for you.
RestClient: A simple tool for calling other services over HTTP.
WebClient: A non-blocking (reactive) tool for calling other services over HTTP.
KafkaTemplate: The tool you use to send messages to Kafka topics.
JdbcTemplate: Run plain SQL easily without the heavy JPA layer.
TransactionTemplate: Start a database transaction in code, when you can't use @Transactional.
ApplicationEventPublisher: Sends an event inside the app so that @EventListener methods run.
ResponseEntity: The full HTTP response: status code, headers and body.
HttpStatus: Named HTTP status codes like CREATED (201) or CONFLICT (409).
DataSource: The connection to the database (usually a pool of connections).
HikariDataSource: A very fast pool of database connections; Spring Boot's default.
AbstractRoutingDataSource: A DataSource that picks which real database to use for each call.
ObjectMapper: Converts Java objects to JSON text and back.
MeterRegistry: Where you record metrics (counters, timers) that dashboards can read.
Mono: A reactive value that will arrive later: zero or one result.
ServerWebExchange: The current request and response inside Spring Cloud Gateway.
GlobalFilter: Code that runs for every request passing through the gateway.
HandlerInterceptor: Code that runs before/after every controller call, like a security guard at the door.
HttpServletRequest: The incoming web request: URL, headers, client IP.
ProceedingJoinPoint: The method call being wrapped. proceed() runs the real method.
ConsumerRecord: One Kafka message with its key, value, topic and offset.
